correctness.rationale: The inverse-square semiaxes are positive and strictly ordered. A plane restriction has exact eigenvalue-ratio eccentricity; all circular normals are classified, and the traceless 2-by-2 gap has a rank-two tangent derivative. Four spherical patches yield the quartic coefficient. Interlacing gives the endpoint, a perfect-square identity proves the sharp lower bound, and a rational decreasing involution plus endpoint behavior proves exactly two inverse preimages away from equality. Exact biaxial CDFs and numerical independent-basis tests cross-check the formulas; finite samples are not used as proofs.

originality.rationale: Hayes (1998) establishes the geometry of the two circular section planes, but not a spherical probability law. Makarenko–Fletcher–Shukurov (2014) analyze full random-cut filamentarity histograms; Landrø (2015) analyzes section aspect-ratio histograms and uses approximate formulas for the triaxial case. Their inspected results do not state the exact fourth-order small-eccentricity tail coefficient, sharp coefficient-versus-maximum inequality, or the complete two-preimage inverse classification. A one-spike-ellipsoid random-radius result covers background axisymmetric distributions only. Exact historical priority is provisional.
residual_risks: Historical priority is provisional: scientific databases are not exhaustive and equivalent probability asymptotics might be stated elsewhere under optical-axis or stereological terminology.

value.rationale: The tail exponent separates triaxial from biaxial section geometry, and an explicit coefficient quantifies rare near-circular observations. The coefficient and maximal eccentricity obey a sharp natural geometric inequality with an intrinsic equality shape; their exact generic two-to-one ambiguity identifies a real boundary of reduced stereological information, complementing full-histogram shape recovery.
